# v2.1.0 — Your Android phone inside Control Code, for you and your agents

Connect a phone or start an emulator and its screen shows up live in a tab. You use it with the mouse and keyboard, and your agents use it the way a person would: they read the screen, tap, swipe, type, open apps and read logcat. This release also fixes freezes in the interface, the browser stealing focus while an agent works, and workspaces that wouldn't open or switch on Ubuntu.

---

## 📱 The Device tab

- **Only if you have adb.** Control Code finds it in `ANDROID_HOME`, your `PATH` or the usual Android SDK folders. Without adb, nothing new appears. Opening the app doesn't start the adb daemon: it starts when you open the tab or an agent uses the device.
- **Live video, straight from adb.** The screen streams as H.264 from `screenrecord`, at up to 60 frames per second, with no app installed on the phone. If the video isn't available, the tab falls back to screenshots.
- **The mouse is your finger.** Click to tap, hold for a long press, drag to drag (you see it move as you drag), and scroll with the wheel. Right-click or Esc goes back, and the keyboard and paste type into the phone.
- **Buttons** for back, home, recents, volume and power, plus a device picker when several are connected.
- **No device?** The tab explains how to connect one, and lists your emulators with a button to start each.
- **One per workspace**, shared by you and your agents. It opens by itself, without taking focus, the first time an agent uses the device.

## 🤖 Agents use the device like a person

13 new MCP tools, offered only when adb is installed:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `android_devices` | Connected devices and emulators, and the emulators you can start |
| `android_emulator` | Starts an emulator and waits for it to boot *(asks first)* |
| `android_snapshot` | The screen as text, with a ref for each element |
| `android_screenshot` | An image of the screen |
| `android_tap`, `android_swipe` | Tap by ref, text or coordinates; long press, double tap; scroll or drag |
| `android_type`, `android_key` | Type into a field (clear first, submit after); press keys |
| `android_app` | Launch, stop, open a URL or deep link, list apps, see what's in front |
| `android_install` | Install an APK, uninstall, clear data *(asks first)* |
| `android_wait` | Wait for text to appear or disappear, or for the screen to settle |
| `android_logcat` | Recent log lines, by app, level or pattern |
| `android_shell` | Any `adb shell` command *(asks first)* |

- **You see who does what.** Every tap and swipe from an agent is drawn on the screen in its color, with a "using the device" banner.
- **No fighting over the phone.** If you touched it in the last few seconds, the agent is told, so it waits or asks you instead of taking over.

**Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO:** MIUI blocks simulated touches until you turn on *USB debugging (Security settings)* in Developer options. The tab tells you when this is needed.

**Known limits:** typing works only with plain ASCII characters (Android's `input` rejects accents and emoji; the tab tells you which ones it skipped), and there's no multitouch (pinch, rotate).

## 🛠️ Fixes

- **No more freezes.** Autosaving tabs no longer sends every terminal's scrollback through the interface, and 88 commands that used to run on the interface thread now run in the background. Terminal output is batched per frame, and closed terminals no longer leave listeners behind.
- **The browser keeps your focus.** While an agent clicks and types in the project's browser, your cursor stays where you left it: in a terminal, the editor or another panel. Scrolling stays inside the page, and an agent's screenshot leaves you on the tab you were looking at.
- **Workspaces on Ubuntu.** Picking a workspace opens it even if the app was closed abruptly last time, switching workspaces brings the right window to the front on Wayland (GNOME), and "Open here" no longer leaves the app without a window. Errors when opening a workspace are now shown instead of failing silently.
